definitions.gloss: to fear, to be afraid of

examples.japanese: ⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{恐|おそ}れる。

examples.english: I'm sorry to trouble you, but...
There's nothing to be afraid of.

notes:
An older godan verb meaning "to fear." In modern Japanese, the ichidan form {恐|おそ}れる is far more common. The godan form {恐|おそ}る survives mainly in set expressions.

FORMS:
- {恐|おそ}る: godan form (archaic/literary)
- {恐|おそ}れる: ichidan form (standard modern usage)

SET EXPRESSIONS:
- {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}ります: I'm sorry to trouble you (very polite, used in business/service)
- {恐|おそ}る{恐|おそ}る: timidly, gingerly (reduplication)
- {恐|おそ}らく: probably, perhaps (adverb derived from this verb)

COMMON PATTERNS (using {恐|おそ}れる):
- {失敗|しっぱい}を{恐|おそ}れる: to fear failure
- {恐|おそ}れることはない: there's nothing to fear

RELATED WORDS:
- {恐|おそ}れ: fear (noun)
- {恐|おそ}ろしい: frightening, terrible (adjective)
- {怖|こわ}い: scary (more colloquial)
